$comment: Crustdata API (version 2025-11-01) to CompanyEnrich V2 migration mapping. Source of truth for the tables in docs/migrate-from-crustdata*.mdx. Validated against openapi/v2.json by scripts/sync-migrations.mjs. Crustdata names come from its public API documentation and OpenAPI reference as checked on checkedAt.

vendor.name: Crustdata
vendor.legacy: The legacy /screener and /data_lab endpoints, which Crustdata replaced with API version 2025-11-01 in May 2026, are not covered.

fidelity.renamed: Same meaning and values under a different name or label.
fidelity.transformed: Same information in a different format, casing, or structure. Convert it in code.
fidelity.lossy: Related but not equivalent. Values can differ, so check the fields your code depends on.

endpoints.note: The company record is the response body, with no `matches` array or `confidence_score`. No match returns `404` and is not charged. The base record covers `basic_info`, `locations`, and `social_profiles`; `funding`, `technographics`, part of `taxonomy`, and `headcount` become expansions, and the other sections have no equivalent. See the field mapping.

Up to 50 domains per request, so send longer lists in chunks of 50. `items` come back in request order, each with the input `domain` in place of `matched_on`, a `status` of `found`, `not-found`, `invalid-domain`, or `pending`, and `company` when `status` is `found`. For up to 10,000 domains in the background, use `POST /v2/companies/enrich/bulk`.

One company per request. Every property you send must match. When several companies match, the highest-ranked one is returned, with no `confidence_score` and no other candidates. No match returns `404` and is not charged.
Crustdata IDs do not carry over. Enrich by the domain stored with the record, or store the CompanyEnrich `id` and use `GET /v2/companies/{companyId}`.

drop.fields: the response is always the full base record.

endpoints.note: There is no separate identify step. Enrichment returns the full company record, or `404` when there is none. One domain per request.

drop.fields: the response is always the full base record.

endpoints.note: Returns the full company record, or `404` when there is none. One profile URL per request.

drop.fields: the response is always the full base record.

endpoints.note: One name per request. Returns the full record of the highest-ranked match, with no `confidence_score` and no other candidates, or `404`. Read `domain` from the record.
Crustdata IDs do not carry over.

drop.fields: results are always full company records.

redesign.sorts: results come in relevance order, so sort in your code.

endpoints.note: Rewrite each filter. See [Translate search filters](/docs/migrate-from-crustdata-search). `pageSize` goes up to 100, against 1,000 for `limit`. Search results carry the same fields as enrichment, so you may not need to enrich them afterwards.

drop.search.mode: semantic search has no mode. For a `lexical` query that must match exact words, use `filter.keywords` or `filter.query` instead.
drop.fields: results are always full company records.

endpoints.note: Send the query as `semantic.query`, with any filters as hard constraints. Results are ranked by relevance, as in Crustdata. By default, the query also sets inferred filters such as location and size; set `semantic.autoFilter` to `false` to rank by it alone. A cursor lasts 24 hours, against 20 minutes for a ranked Crustdata search.
Free. Search responses carry no total, so send the same filter to the count endpoint.

Free. Company autocomplete suggests companies for a domain prefix or URL, so it covers `basic_info.primary_domain` only. For other fields, use `GET /v2/technologies/autocomplete`, `GET /v2/keywords/autocomplete`, `GET /v2/industries`, or the geo endpoints. Company names have no lookup.

redesign.webhook_url: there are no webhooks. Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the job completes.

endpoints.note: Background job for up to 10,000 domains. Domains only. Download the results as JSON, NDJSON, or CSV. See [Bulk jobs and exports](/docs/bulk-jobs-and-exports). For up to 50 domains, `POST /v2/companies/enrich/batch` answers in the same request.
Bulk jobs take domains only. Call `POST /v2/companies/enrich` per name or profile URL within your rate limit.

redesign.webhook_url: there are no webhooks. Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the export completes.

endpoints.note: Exports every result of a search as a background job. Poll the batch, then download JSON, NDJSON, or CSV.
No live search. Search the CompanyEnrich index with `POST /v2/companies/search`. Live filter names such as `REGION` need a full rewrite.

drop.fields: results are always full person records.
drop.explain: a debug flag. Use the free count endpoint to test conditions one at a time.

redesign.sorts: results come in relevance order, so sort in your code.
redesign.post_processing: drop excluded profiles or names from the results in your code.
redesign.preview: use the free `POST /v2/people/search/preview` or count endpoint instead.

endpoints.note: Rewrite person conditions as `filter` and employer conditions as a `company` query. See [Translate search filters](/docs/migrate-from-crustdata-search#people-search-patterns). Results are full person records, so you do not need to enrich them by profile URL afterwards.

drop.mode: semantic search has no recall mode.

endpoints.note: The plain-language query infers person filters and employers, such as `marketing leaders at Series B fintech startups in London`. There is no relevance `fit` tier per result.
Free. Search responses carry no total.

No person lookup by profile URL. With a work email, use `POST /v2/people/enrich`. Without one, search by name at the employer's domain with `POST /v2/people/search`, which returns candidates without a confidence score. If your code searches and then enriches each result, drop the enrich step: search results are full records.

One work email per request. The API resolves the company from the email domain, then matches the person. The full person record is the response body. No match returns `404` and is not charged, in place of a `match_status` of `not_found` or `redacted`. Personal emails have no equivalent, so a call whose callers can send personal emails needs redesign.
No lookup by profile URL or Google Scholar URL.

Takes a CompanyEnrich person ID, not a profile URL or a business email. After a people search or `POST /v2/people/enrich`, pass each person's `id`. A call that has only a profile URL has no equivalent. One person per request. Returns one work email with a `status` and `certainty`. Costs 10 credits only when it finds an email your account has not accessed before.
No personal emails, phone numbers, or websites.
Free. Suggests job titles for the `position` filter. Seniority and department take fixed values, listed in the field mapping. Other fields have no lookup.

redesign.webhook_url: there are no webhooks. Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the export completes.

endpoints.note: Exports every result of a people search as a background job.
No bulk person enrichment. Call `POST /v2/people/enrich` per work email within your rate limit, or export a people search.
No live search or live profile retrieval.
No work-history verification.

List jobs with `GET /v2/batches` and cancel one with `POST /v2/batches/{id}/cancel`. Download the results of a bulk enrichment or an export from its own results endpoint, such as `GET /v2/companies/enrich/bulk/{id}/results`, as JSON, NDJSON, or CSV, instead of a gzipped JSONL file.

Free. Returns your credit totals and plan capabilities. See [Account fields](/docs/migrate-from-crustdata-field-mapping#account-fields). Each paid response also carries `x-credit-cost` and `x-credit-remaining` headers, in place of `X-Credits-Used`.
No usage or permissions API. Log `x-credit-cost` per call, and read plan limits from `capabilities` on `GET /v2/me`.
No job postings. Workforce history is headcount by department, not postings.
No social posts.
No web search or page fetch.

No watches, notifications, or webhooks. To track changes, re-enrich the companies you follow on a schedule and compare `updatedAt`, headcount, or funding. To find new matches, re-run a search and compare IDs.
No agent search. Semantic company and people search take a plain-language query, and the MCP server lets your own agent chain calls.

mcp.note: By domain, or by name or social profile. The record includes technologies, keywords, and funding.
Headcount by department, with monthly history.
Filters, a plain-language description, or 1 to 10 seed domains for lookalikes.
By name, title, seniority, department, country, and employer.

mcp.crustdata: Enrich a person or identify one from an email
mcp.note: By work email, or by a CompanyEnrich person ID from search. No lookup by profile URL.

Crustdata returns the self-reported range from the company profile. CompanyEnrich `employees` is calculated from its employee data, and the self-reported range is a search filter only, `reportedEmployees`.
Employees observed in CompanyEnrich data. Without the expansion, read the `employees` range.
From `GET /v2/companies/workforce`, one point per month.
From `GET /v2/companies/workforce`.
Not returned. Compare two history points from `GET /v2/companies/workforce`. To filter on growth, use the `workforceGrowth` search filter.
Counts for 14 departments instead of Crustdata's functions. Divide by `workforce.observedEmployeeCount` for shares.
From `GET /v2/companies/workforce`, by department.
A range label, such as `10m-50m`, instead of two bounds. Crustdata returns `0` for no estimate; CompanyEnrich returns `null`.
One symbol instead of a list. `financial.stockExchange` holds the exchange.
A label such as `Series A`, where Crustdata returns `series_a`. The labels are not a fixed list, so map them to your own values if your code compares them.
A date-time instead of a date.
Take the latest round by `date`. The amount is a string.

Listed per round, as text.
A country name in source casing, or an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Crustdata filters take alpha-3 codes, such as `USA`.

Crustdata holds a full location string. Build one from the city, state, and country objects if you need it.
Headquarters only.
A list of industries. Values can differ.
A list of codes instead of one primary code. Crustdata codes come from the 2022 NAICS edition, and a few codes changed between editions.
CompanyEnrich `industry` is a NAICS industry title, such as `Software Publishers`.
Keywords that describe what the company does, from different sources.
No SIC codes or NAICS level titles. The first two, three, or four digits of a NAICS code give its sector, sub-sector, or industry group.
